title: The Cathedral of Joy
summary: One-on-one with Alfredo Jaar, Damien Hirst’s secret life, Anish Kapoor's optical trickery, and another BS "most influential" list.

title: No One Is Accountable in Taryn Simon’s Detective Story
summary: In her ambitious exhibition at the Guggenheim Museum, injustice seems purely systemic, not the result of individuals behaving badly.

title: Buffalo Puppet Procession Traces Native History Through NYC’s Streets
summary: “Return of the Buffalo: Tatanka Owe Akupi” pays homage to 38 Dakota men executed by President Abraham Lincoln in Mankato, Minnesota, in 1862.

title: NYC’s Shelter Population Speaks Out in Public Art Project
summary: Alex Strada’s “Public Address” brings handwritten testimonies from over 400 unhoused New Yorkers and shelter staff to a dozen locations across the Bronx.

title: The Titillating Tale of Damien Hirst’s Gay Hole
summary: An infectious play by Sleth explores infatuation and fame through an imagined relationship between Hirst and his gay lover, a younger artist whose paintings consist of holes on the ground.

title: What “The Book of Genocides” Teaches Us
summary: Dana Mashoian Walrath’s work of graphic nonfiction points to historical patterns across 10 genocides, from Germany and Turkey to Gaza.

title: Liu Wei’s Met Facade Comission Reflects Our Moment
summary: On view through next June, Liu's sculpture series “Speculation” (2026) contemplates the contradictory elements of collapse and civic transformation.

title: Leon Black Plans to Turn Woolworth Mansion Into His Own Museum, Book Reveals
summary: The disgraced financier, whose ties to Jeffrey Epstein are being investigated in Congress, told author William D. Cohan that he wants to turn the Manhattan property into “his version of the Neue Galerie.”

title: Borusan Contemporary Presents Two New Exhibitions
summary: From “the act of looking” to intelligent technologies, “Olivo Barbieri: Time Space Geometry” and “Haunted” explore how images shape our perception of reality. Opening September 19, 2026.

title: A View From the Easel
summary: “Piles to start a project, piles during a project, and piles of stuff after it is finished.”

title: Ed Sheeran Should Stop Thinking Out Loud
summary: Artists skewer the singer for dropping his pro-Palestine openers, tiny hot dogs at Affordable Art Fair, and the bizarre selections of TIME100 Art.

title: The Best and the Absolute Worst of the TIME 100 List
summary: Amy Sherald shines on the magazine’s uneven list, Artadia names a new director, Johnny Depp's awfulness, and more in Art Movements.

title: A Tiny Hot Dog Art Show and Other Treasures at Affordable Art Fair
summary: Dylan Martinez's glass-blown water balloons, Deanna Billy Projects' mini wiener paintings, and Abu Oluwaseyi's abstract portraits all caught my eye at this year’s NYC edition.

title: Artists Fear Displacement as ChaShaMa Forced to Vacate Studios
summary: The organization will lose half of its studio spaces to a tenant who wants to expand their footprint in the Brooklyn Army Terminal building.

title: African-American Blacksmiths Forge a Lineage of Sankofa
summary: Blacksmiths in the South have long embedded West African symbolism into gates, rails, and window bars, proof that the craft evolved with every hand that held the hammer.
